entry.title: Ravda Beach, Nessebar
entry.summary: Ravda is a quieter resort village south of Nessebar with a long sandy beach and shallow water. It is more relaxed than Sunny Beach, with a mix of hotels, restaurants and local life.

entry.title: Golden Sands Beach, Varna
entry.summary: Golden Sands is one of the largest Bulgarian resorts, set inside a nature park north of Varna. The beach is a wide band of fine sand with shallow water, and there are many bars, rides and water sports.

entry.title: Primorsko Beach, Primorsko
entry.summary: Primorsko is a resort town on the southern Black Sea coast with long sandy beaches, shallow water and a seafront promenade. It is popular with families and young people and has forested hills behind.

entry.title: Pomorie Beach, Pomorie
entry.summary: Pomorie sits on a narrow peninsula, and its sandy beaches are lined with groynes and backed by apartments and promenades. The town is known for its salt lake and mineral spa, and it is quieter than Sunny Beach.

entry.title: Saints Constantine and Helena Beach, Varna
entry.summary: Saints Constantine and Helena is the oldest seaside resort in Bulgaria, set in a park north of Varna. The beaches are small and sandy and sit below hotels and gardens, with a relaxed spa-resort feel.

entry.title: Varna City Beach, Varna
entry.summary: Varna city beach is a long strip of sand below the Sea Garden, within walking distance of the centre. It is easy to reach and lively in summer, and the water can be wavy when the wind blows from the east.

entry.title: Byala Beach, Byala
entry.summary: Byala is a small town on the northern Black Sea coast with a sandy beach, a wooden pier and calm water. It is low-key, with a harbour feel and fewer large hotels than the main resorts.

entry.title: Chernomorets Beach, Sozopol
entry.summary: Chernomorets is a village beach north of Sozopol with a long curve of sand and rows of sunbeds below a low headland. It is quieter than the big resorts and suits families who want shallow water.

entry.title: Vlas Beach, Sveti Vlas
entry.summary: Sveti Vlas is a resort town at the northern end of Sunny Beach bay, with a sandy beach edged by rocks and dune grass. It is calmer than Sunny Beach and sits below the green slopes of the Balkan foothills.

entry.title: Silistar Beach, Tsarevo
entry.summary: Silistar is a quiet sandy beach on the far southern coast, close to the Strandzha Nature Park and the Turkish border region. It has a simple, uncrowded feel, with forested hills behind and few buildings nearby.

entry.title: Kavatsite Beach, Sozopol
entry.summary: Kavatsite is a long sandy beach north of Sozopol, backed by dunes and a pine camping area. The water is shallow and calm, and the atmosphere is relaxed and informal.

entry.title: Krapets Beach, Shabla
entry.summary: Krapets is a small village on the northern coast near Shabla with a long sandy beach and few visitors. It is simple and low-key, with calm water in summer and a very different feel from the big resorts.

entry.title: Arkutino Beach, Primorsko
entry.summary: Arkutino is a sandy beach between Sozopol and Primorsko, set next to Arkutino lake and the Ropotamo nature reserve. It is calmer than the resort strips, with dunes and pines behind the sand.

entry.title: Obzor Beach, Obzor
entry.summary: Obzor has a long sandy beach with a relaxed resort feel, a seafront promenade, restaurants and low-rise hotels. It is quieter than Sunny Beach, and the water is shallow near the shore.

entry.title: Veleka Beach, Sinemorets
entry.summary: Near Sinemorets, the Veleka river reaches the Black Sea inside the Strandzha Nature Park. The beach is a long strip of sand with the river on one side and forested hills behind, and it feels wilder than the northern resorts.

entry.title: Irakli Beach, Obzor
entry.summary: Irakli is a long, undeveloped sandy beach south of Obzor, backed by the forested hills of the Emine cape. It has no hotels, so it feels wild. Most visitors arrive on a path from the road, and part of the beach is known as an informal naturist spot.

entry.title: Kiten Beach, Kiten
entry.summary: Kiten is a small resort on the southern coast with fine sand and calmer surroundings than the big northern resorts. Its beaches are backed by a mix of small hotels and campsites.

entry.title: Albena Beach, Balchik
entry.summary: Albena is a purpose-built resort north of Varna with a broad, gently sloping sandy beach backed by dunes and woodland. The water is shallow and the beach is well kept, which makes it popular with families.

entry.title: Sunny Beach, Nessebar
entry.summary: Sunny Beach is the largest resort on the Bulgarian Black Sea, with about eight kilometres of wide golden sand and shallow water. It is lively, with beach bars, water sports and sunbeds along the main stretch, and quieter corners at the far northern and southern ends.

entry.title: Assos Beach, Behramkale
entry.summary: Assos is a stone village on a hill above the northern Aegean, with the ruins of a Temple of Athena at the top and a small harbour below. The pebble coast at the foot of the village is quiet and quaint, and it makes a calm stop on the north Aegean route.

entry.title: Marmaris Beach, Mugla
entry.summary: Marmaris Beach lies along the sheltered bay at Marmaris, with a long seafront of sand and pebbles. The town, marina and castle are close by, and boats run from here to coves and beaches around the bay.

entry.title: Side Beach, Manavgat
entry.summary: Side has long beaches of fine sand on both sides of a small peninsula holding the ancient town and the Temple of Apollo. The water is shallow and gentle, and the old streets, shops and ruins are a short walk from the sand.

entry.title: Beldibi Beach, Kemer
entry.summary: Beldibi is a pebble beach between Antalya and Kemer, with the Taurus Mountains rising steeply behind the coast. The sea is clear, and the shore has fewer crowds than the central resort beaches.

entry.title: Dikili Beach, Izmir
entry.summary: Dikili is a small Aegean town north of Izmir, with a beach that looks across the water toward the Greek island of Lesbos. It is mostly visited by Turkish holidaymakers, so the atmosphere is local and calm.

entry.title: Datca Beach, Mugla
entry.summary: Datca is a laid-back town at the western end of a long peninsula between the Aegean and the Mediterranean. The town beach has clear water and is backed by cafes and small shops, and the pace is slower than in nearby Marmaris or Bodrum.

entry.title: Adrasan Beach, Kumluca
entry.summary: Adrasan is a calm bay in a green valley on the Lycian coast, with a pebble beach and a few small pensions and restaurants. Boat trips run from the bay to Suluada island, and the village feels far quieter than the large resorts near Antalya.

entry.title: Badavut Beach, Ayvalik
entry.summary: Badavut is a sandy beach on the Aegean coast near Ayvalik, in the north of the Turkish Aegean. The setting is calmer than the big southern resorts, with olive groves inland and a relaxed local atmosphere.

entry.title: Altinkum Beach, Didim
entry.summary: Altinkum is a wide, golden sandy beach in Didim on the Aegean coast, with very shallow water that suits young children. Its name means golden sand in Turkish, and the town behind the beach has hotels, cafes and shops.

entry.title: Gumusluk Beach, Bodrum
entry.summary: Gumusluk is a quiet fishing village on the west of the Bodrum peninsula, with a small sandy beach and a bay sheltered by an islet. Seafood restaurants sit directly on the water, and the setting is a calm alternative to the busier resort towns.

entry.title: Akyaka Beach, Mugla
entry.summary: Akyaka is a village at the head of Gokova Bay, known for traditional wooden houses and a cold river that meets the sea. The beach is calm and sheltered, and the area suits a quiet, low-key stay.
